braille.notes: Numbered lines 4-18 (a genuine excerpt). Field width 5, stripped. Lines 1-2 (source 4-5): lead-in paragraph, cell 3. Line 3 (6): blank. Line 4 (7): salutation, cell 3. Lines 5-9 (8-12): letter body, first line cell 5, runovers cell 3. Line 10 (13): signature, cell 7. Line 11 (14): blank. Lines 12-15 (15-18): resuming narrative paragraph, cell 3.

resolution: A and B transcribed identical `braille.lines`, verified byte-for-byte against lines 7091-7105 after stripping the 5-character line-number field (the '(Return to Text)' line 7106 excluded). Structural disagreement: A gave the salutation, body and signature as three separate print.blocks (matching the braille's own three distinct indents -- cell3/cell5-runover-cell3/cell7); B merged all three into a single 'quote' block's text (joined with literal newlines), which would build as one continuously-wrapped paragraph and lose the signature's own distinct cell-7 attribution position entirely. Resolved to A's three-block structure, since it reflects what the agreed braille actually shows (three differently-indented pieces, not one wrapped block), and keeps the signature as a genuine `attribution` block consistent with 9.7.1b's own instruction to move it to the attribution position.
